overview: Russia is the largest country in the world by area, stretching across Eastern Europe and northern Asia. Its capital and largest city is Moscow. Russia was the largest republic of the Soviet Union, which broke up in 1991, and it is one of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council. Since 2014 Russia has occupied parts of Ukraine, and in 2022 it launched a full-scale invasion of the country.

geography.text: Russia spans 11 time zones, from the Baltic Sea to the Pacific Ocean. The Ural Mountains separate European Russia, where most people live, from Siberia, a vast region of forest, frozen tundra and great rivers such as the Ob, the Yenisei and the Lena. Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest lake in the world, and the Volga is the longest river in Europe.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Very cold winters across most of the country, especially in Siberia, with warm summers in the south.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Siberian tigers, brown bears, polar bears and the Baikal seal, which lives only in Lake Baikal.

history.text: Russia grew from the medieval state of Kievan Rus' and the later Grand Duchy of Moscow into a vast empire stretching to the Pacific. The tsars were overthrown in 1917, and the Bolsheviks created the Soviet Union, which lost tens of millions of people in the Second World War and became a superpower. When the Soviet Union broke up in 1991, Russia became its successor state.

events.title: Christianity adopted
events.text: Grand Prince Volodymyr of Kyiv adopts Orthodox Christianity.

events.title: First tsar
events.text: Ivan IV, 'the Terrible', is crowned tsar.

events.title: St Petersburg founded
events.text: Peter the Great builds a new capital on the Baltic.

events.title: Revolution
events.text: The tsar is overthrown and the Bolsheviks seize power.

events.title: Soviet Union breaks up
events.text: The fifteen Soviet republics become independent.

government.text: Russia is officially a federal semi-presidential republic, but power is concentrated in the President, who appoints the Prime Minister. Vladimir Putin has been President or Prime Minister since 1999. Opposition politicians and independent media face severe restrictions, and constitutional changes in 2020 allow him to stay in office until 2036. Russia has a permanent seat with a veto on the UN Security Council.

economy.text: Russia has huge reserves of oil, gas, coal, metals and timber, and energy exports have long paid for much of the state budget. It is also a major exporter of wheat and weapons. Since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Western countries have imposed wide-ranging sanctions, and Russia sells more of its oil to China and India.

culture.text: Russia has produced some of the world's most famous writers, including Tolstoy, Dostoevsky and Chekhov, and composers such as Tchaikovsky. Russian ballet, especially at the Bolshoi and Mariinsky theatres, is world-renowned. The Trans-Siberian Railway, at about 9,300 kilometres, is the longest railway line in the world.

items.title: Swan Lake
items.text: Tchaikovsky's ballet, first performed in Moscow in 1877.

items.title: Red Square
items.text: Moscow's central square, beside the Kremlin and St Basil's Cathedral.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Borscht, blini pancakes and pelmeni dumplings are popular.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Russian literature, ballet and classical music are world-famous, from Tolstoy to Tchaikovsky.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Maslenitsa, a week of pancakes before Lent, ends with burning a straw figure of winter.

sport.text: Russia has long been a sporting power in ice hockey, gymnastics, figure skating and chess. It hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics and the 2018 World Cup. Because of doping and later the invasion of Ukraine, its teams were banned from many international competitions.

items.text: Russia hosted the men's World Cup.

items.title: Chess
items.text: Russian and Soviet players held the world title for most of the 1900s.

didYouKnow: Lake Baikal in Siberia holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.

keyPeople.name: Dmitri Mendeleev
keyPeople.text: Created the periodic table of the elements.
